title: Granular cohort A/B experiment runner with drift-aware stopping and auto-rollback hooks
creator: Priya Patel
description: Build a first-class A/B experimentation runner that supports fine-grained cohort targeting, progressive exposure, sequential statistical checks, drift detection, and automated rollback hooks. This product ticket scopes the UX, API surface, safety thresholds, and evaluation metrics required to run safe model version experiments across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The runner should be accessible from Redwood Console and via the Redwood API/SDK. Key goals: 1) reduce manual effort for PM/Eng to create experiments, 2) surface statistically meaningful signals early while controlling false positives, 3) provide guardrails and automatic rollback when regressions are detected, 4) allow shadow traffic and canary splits for risk mitigation.
acceptance_criteria: Console: Create experiment flow for model version A/B, supporting cohort selectors (user attributes, region, route) and percent exposure ramps
API: REST endpoint POST /experiments accepts target_model, control_model, cohorts, exposure_schedule, primary_metrics, alert_rules, and rollback_policy
Stat testing: Implements group sequential testing with alpha spending (e.g., O'Brien-Fleming) and minimum sample thresholds to guard against early stopping bias
Drift: Real-time distribution drift detector on embedding and response features that can trigger pause or rollback when drift exceeds configured thresholds
Auto-rollback: Configurable rollback hooks that can automatically shift traffic back to control and open an incident runbook when regressions exceed high-severity thresholds
Shadowing: Support 100% shadow traffic mode with safe logging (PII redaction) and no user-facing impact
Monitoring: Experiment dashboard shows converging metrics, p-values, confidence intervals, and cohort breakdowns with latency/cost tradeoffs
Audit: Every experiment run produces an immutable audit record with config, rollouts, decisions, and links to PRs/dashboards
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): API prototype + minimal console create flow; wire up to runtime routing to split traffic at edge for Hosted only
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Add sequential testing engine, dashboard visualizations, and shadow traffic ingestion pipeline; integrate with Dedicated routing
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Drift detectors, auto-rollback hooks, and privacy-safe logs for Private deployments; compliance sign-off
Phase 4 (1 week): E2E QA, runbook creation, early customer pilot, and postmortem template
monitoring_and_metrics: Primary metrics: correctness/quality (task-dependent), latency P50/P95, per-token cost
Secondary metrics: rate of OOMs, error counts, throughput per GPU, tail latencies
Safety signals: toxic content rate, hallucination proxies, abuse detection counts
Stat outputs: sequential p-values, cumulative sample counts, confidence intervals, stopping boundary state
Operational: experiment uptime, rollback count, time-to-rollback, alert noise rate
test_plan: Unit tests for exposure scheduler and cohort selector logic
Integration test: synthetic traffic through runtime router verifying split percentages and shadow logging
Stat test harness: simulate uplift/regression scenarios to verify false positive control and stopping behavior
Privacy QA: verify logs redact PII and that shadow traffic cannot affect user-visible outputs
Chaos scenario: partial region outage should gracefully degrade experiments and follow fallback policy
notes: Design trade-off: conservative sequential stopping reduces speed of rollout but lowers risk of false rollback; configurable alpha spending to allow teams to choose sensitivity
We should reuse existing rollout metadata and audit logging infrastructure from console-2025.02
Estimate assumes ENG-21458 (runtime split router) implements per-route hashing and KV pass-through for experiment trace IDs
Consider exposing a lightweight SDK helper for client-side cohort assignment to ensure deterministic bucketing across regions
